summary: Ambrogio Ballini (1879–1950) was an Indologist who studied at Bologna, Milan under Ascoli, Padua under Teza, and Bonn under Jacobi. He held Sanskrit chairs at Padua (1913), Catholic University of the Sacred Heart (1924), and Sapienza University of Rome (1941–1949).

Amelia Bonea is a historian and Indologist. She earned a BA from the University of Tokyo (2001–2007) and a PhD from Heidelberg University (2008–2012). Her posts include Oxford (2012–2017), Heidelberg (2018–2022), and Manchester (c. 2019).

Amelia Hall is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford in 2012. Her attested appointments in 2019 include Naropa University and Central Michigan University.
Ameneh Shirazinejad works in Buddhist and religious studies. She has held posts as an Arabic language tutor at George Washington University and as a Visiting Fellow at the University of Delhi.

Amin Sweeney (1938–2010) was a linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of London (c. 1967–1970). He taught at the National University of Malaysia (1970–1977) and served as professor and department chair at UC Berkeley (1986–1991).
Amita Chatterjee is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. She served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University, where she is attested in 1999 and 2009.
Amod Jayant Lele is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Parimal G. Patil.

Amrit Madhav Ghatage (1913–2003) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor and Head of Linguistics at Deccan College (c. 1961–1978) and Vice-President of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute until 2003.

Amrita Saikia works in Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (2018–2022), where she also held research and teaching posts, and held appointments at Woxsen University (2022) and GIGA (2023–2024).

Amrith Krishna works in linguistics and Indology. He has held positions at IIT Kharagpur, University of Cambridge, IT University of Copenhagen, Oriflow, Uniphore (attested 2023), and Learno.AI (attested 2024–2025).
Amruta Barbadikar works in computational linguistics and Indology. She completed her PhD in 2020 at the University of Hyderabad, where she also held an academic post.
Amy Heller is a Tibetologist and historian. She earned a PhD from EPHE under Ariane Macdonald and held positions at Yale, CNRS, Sapienza University of Rome, SOAS, INALCO, and the University of Bern.

Amy L. Allocco is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Colgate University, Harvard University, and Emory University (PhD 2001–2009), and held a post at Elon University (attested 2015).

Amy Paris Langenberg specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She received her PhD from Columbia University (c. 2001–2008) and held posts at Brown University, Auburn University, and Eckerd College.

Amy Sims Miller is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Virginia (PhD 2004 under David Germano), alongside training under several traditional teachers.

Amy Snyder Ohta is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology. She completed her studies at the University of California, Los Angeles (1990, 1993) and became a professor at the University of Washington (c. 1995).
Ana Agud is a linguist and Indologist. She studied at the University of Salamanca (PhD 1965–1978) and the University of Tübingen, and became a professor at the University of Salamanca in 1979.

Anagarika Dharmapala (1864–1933) was an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at schools including S. Thomas' College and Royal College, Colombo, he founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 and the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

Anagarika Govinda (1898–1985) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He held a doctorate from Freiburg, founded the Arya Maitreya Mandala (1933), and taught at Visva-Bharati, Patna, Allahabad, Lucknow, and Banaras Hindu University.

Anagarika Munindra (1915–2003) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. He studied under Mahasi Sayadaw and Satya Narayan Goenka, and served as superintendent at the Mahabodhi Temple from 1953 to 1957.
